name: Microsoft

summary.text: Microsoft Corporation is a computer technology company founded on April 4, 1975, by Bill Gates and Paul Allen, originally in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and based in Redmond, Washington after 1986. It is best known for the Windows operating system, the Office software suite, the Xbox brand, and the Azure cloud platform. It has been a public company since its 1986 IPO and files annual (10-K) and quarterly (10-Q) reports with the SEC.

facts.claim: Microsoft was founded on April 4, 1975, by childhood friends Bill Gates and Paul Allen.
facts.quote: On April 4, 1975, at a time when most Americans used typewriters, childhood friends Bill Gates and Paul Allen found Microsoft, a company that makes computer software.

facts.claim: Paul Allen and Bill Gates developed BASIC for the MITS Altair 8800 after the January 1975 Popular Electronics cover inspired them, and sold Altair BASIC to MITS of Albuquerque, which Microsoft's own timeline describes as its first customer.
facts.quote: February 1, 1975 Bill Gates and Paul Allen complete Altair BASIC and sell it to Microsoft’s first customer, MITS of Albuquerque, New Mexico .

facts.claim: Microsoft's company history in its own timeline states that Gates and Allen signed a licensing agreement with MITS on July 22, 1975, before the name Microsoft was chosen and before it was an official partnership.
facts.quote: July 22, 1975 Paul Allen and Bill Gates sign a licensing agreement with MITS regarding the Basic Interpreter. The name Microsoft has not yet been chosen, and Microsoft is not yet an official partnership.

facts.claim: The company was originally called Micro-Soft, a portmanteau of microprocessors and software, and was based in Albuquerque, New Mexico, before relocating to Washington State in 1979.
facts.quote: Originally based in Albuquerque, New Mexico , Microsoft relocated to Washington State in 1979 and eventually grew into a major multinational technology corporation.

facts.claim: In 1981, Microsoft licensed its MS-DOS operating system to IBM for IBM's first personal computer.
facts.quote: The company went on to license its MS-DOS operating system to IBM for its first personal computer, which debuted in 1981.

facts.claim: Microsoft went public in 1986 at $21 a share, raising $61 million, and moved its headquarters to Redmond, Washington.
facts.quote: The following year, the company moved its headquarters to Redmond, Washington, and went public at $21 a share, raising $61 million.

facts.claim: In 1998, the U.S. Department of Justice and 20 state attorneys general charged Microsoft with violating antitrust laws; in 2001 the company reached a settlement with the government that imposed restrictions on its corporate practices.
facts.quote: In 1998, the U.S. Department of Justice and 20 state attorneys general charged Microsoft with violating antitrust laws by using its dominance to drive competitors out of business; in 2001, the company reached a settlement with the government that imposed restrictions on its corporate practices.

facts.claim: Microsoft's investor relations site lists its recent quarterly and annual SEC filings for fiscal years 2025 and 2026, including Forms 10-Q and 10-K.
facts.quote: Recent quarterly and annual filings are available from this web site in Microsoft Word format. Expanded and historical information is available from a third-party web site.

facts.claim: Microsoft filed a Form 10-K annual report on July 29, 2026, which Microsoft's SEC filings index describes as a comprehensive overview of the company for the past year.
facts.quote: Jul 29, 2026 10-K Annual report which provides a comprehensive overview of the company for the past year

facts.claim: Microsoft's security team reported that Storm-0558, a China-based threat actor that Microsoft assessed with moderate confidence, used forged authentication tokens to access email of about 25 organizations, including government agencies, beginning May 15, 2023; Microsoft said no other environment was impacted.
facts.quote: Beginning May 15, 2023, Storm-0558 used forged authentication tokens to access user email from approximately 25 organizations, including government agencies and related consumer accounts in the public cloud. No other environment was impacted.

sources.title: Analysis of Storm-0558 techniques for unauthorized email access

facts.claim: Under the January 23, 2023 extended partnership announced by OpenAI, Microsoft made a multi-year, multi-billion dollar investment in OpenAI, following earlier investments in 2019 and 2021, and Azure remains the exclusive cloud provider for all OpenAI workloads.
facts.quote: This multi-year, multi-billion dollar investment from Microsoft follows their previous investments in 2019 and 2021, and will allow us to continue our independent research and develop AI that is increasingly safe, useful, and powerful.

connections.claim: Bill Gates and Paul Allen co-founded Microsoft on April 4, 1975.
connections.quote: On April 4, 1975, at a time when most Americans used typewriters, childhood friends Bill Gates and Paul Allen found Microsoft, a company that makes computer software.

connections.claim: Microsoft made a multi-year, multi-billion dollar investment in OpenAI in January 2023, extending a partnership in which Azure is the exclusive cloud provider for OpenAI workloads.
connections.quote: This multi-year, multi-billion dollar investment from Microsoft follows their previous investments in 2019 and 2021 ... Azure will remain the exclusive cloud provider for all OpenAI workloads across our research, API and products.
